subject: Science
title: Growth and stem cells
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 7.88 on 996 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 13.88 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to explain how cells divide and then take on different jobs for growth and repair.
success_criteria: I can distinguish making more cells from cells taking on a specialised job.
I can compare animal growth with plant growth.
I can identify a role for an animal stem cell or a plant meristem.

vocab.definition: a cell becoming specialised for a particular job
vocab.example: A developing skin cell differentiates to do a job in skin.

vocab.definition: a cell that can divide and form specialised cell types
vocab.example: Some adult stem cells make replacement blood cells.

vocab.definition: a plant region whose cells divide to make new cells
vocab.example: A root tip contains a meristem.

vocab.definition: an increase in size, including by making more cells
vocab.example: A shoot grows as its cells divide and elongate.

retrieval.question: What two matching products follow body-cell mitosis and cell splitting?
retrieval.answer: Two daughter body cells with the same chromosome set.

retrieval.question: Which process moves particles from low to high concentration using energy?
In which part of a eukaryotic animal cell are chromosomes found?

worked_example.full: In skin, mitosis adds cells; some stem-cell descendants differentiate for a tissue job. At a shoot tip, meristem cells divide, then elongate and differentiate.
worked_example.faded: Skin: mitosis adds cells → differentiation gives a job. Shoot: meristem adds cells → ________ lengthens cells → differentiation.
worked_example.removed_step: Elongation increases the length of plant cells during growth.
worked_example.fade_next: Next time hide the animal differentiation arrow too; pupils explain both missing growth steps with the model.

cfu.question: Show me: does making more cells on its own mean those cells now have a specialised job?
cfu.answer: No; cell differentiation gives specialised roles.

hinge.question: A gut-lining cell and a nerve cell share inherited DNA but have different structures. Which explanation fits this new pair?

options.text: A. They differentiated into specialised cells with different jobs.
B. One cell must have lost every inherited gene.
options.diagnosis: Assumes specialisation requires losing all inherited genes.

options.text: C. Both cells must perform exactly the same job.
options.diagnosis: Confuses shared DNA with identical cell functions.

options.text: D. Neither cell can have developed through cell division.
options.diagnosis: Assumes differentiated cells could not have arisen after cell division.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more correct: proceed; otherwise re-model a dividing stem cell and one specialised skin-cell branch with two paper cards, then ask the parallel hinge. No auto-grade.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A muscle cell and a liver cell share inherited DNA. Must their jobs be identical? Answer: no; differentiation produces specialised cell types.

misconceptions.misconception: New cells must lose their DNA to specialise.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses B, claiming one cell lost every inherited gene.
misconceptions.correction: Both branches keep DNA; differentiation means a different job, not loss of all DNA.

misconceptions.misconception: Cell division alone is sufficient to make specialised tissue.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses C, claiming the two specialised cells must have the same job.
misconceptions.correction: Place a second card for differentiation; in plants include elongation as a further growth step.

we_do.support: Use two labelled branches (animal tissue and plant tip); pupils place the missing elongation card and point to the corresponding change.
we_do.stretch: Explain why a shoot can increase in length even after the division step has ended.

tiers.F: Place divide, elongate and differentiate cards on the skin/shoot branches; omit elongate on the skin branch.
tiers.M: Explain why mitosis alone does not give a new cell its specialised tissue job.
tiers.H: Compare growth in animal tissue with a plant shoot, including an appropriate stem-cell region and what each process adds.

stems.F: In the shoot, first cells …; then they …
stems.M: More cells are made by …, but a job develops when …
stems.H: Both organisms …; however, the plant also … because …

tiers.go_deeper: A tissue gains more cells but no new cell types. What does the model explain, and what is missing?
tiers.early_finisher: Correct a diagram labelling new skin cells “stem cell”; justify two changes.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Scaffolding: Offer a two-branch, high-contrast strip; remove only one cue before asking the pupil to complete it.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Flexible grouping: Quiet pair rehearsal of the same comparison before any written route; point, sign or AAC accepted.
adaptations.semh: Cognitive/metacognitive strategies: Privately preview the top comparison, agree a pause signal, then return to one card.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Technology: Offer large easy-grip model cards; speech-to-text or a photo of the labelled model can capture the response.
adaptations.eal: Explicit instruction: Show the four science words with picture and example sentences; allow planning in any language. Keep M and H scientific demand available.

ta_focus.i_do: “Watch the model. Point to what makes more cells, then what gives one cell a job.”
ta_focus.we_do: “One step is blank. Which part of the shoot becomes longer?”
ta_focus.independent: “Which branch is your comparison about? Show the last step you know.”

prompt_ladder: Wait five seconds; watch for an unaided card choice.
Point to the last completed branch or visual cue.
Ask “Which step makes more cells, and which gives a job?”
Model only the placement of the mitosis card; pupil places the next card.
Finish one branch together; pupil tries the other branch independently.

F.q: What is the plant growth region called?
Which word means a cell gains a particular job?

M.q: Why is division alone not enough for a specialised tissue?
M.a: New cells also need to differentiate.

M.q: What can also happen to plant cells as a shoot grows?

H.q: How are plant and animal growth alike and different?
H.a: Both involve division and differentiation; plant growth also includes cell elongation.

H.q: Why cannot one permanent stem-cell label describe every mature new skin cell?
H.a: Some daughter cells differentiate into specialised types.

facts.claim: Embryonic stem cells may give rise to specialised nerve, muscle and blood cells; plant meristems are regions of cell division at growing shoot and root tips. The pictured cells are examples of possible descendants, not a single cell changing into all three at once.
